independent.summary: `readIn`'s `perNamespace.size === 1` fallback still resolves a BARE host across a namespace boundary: a pod in `prod` whose env holds `redis://cache:6379` gets a `Calls` edge to a `cache` that lives only in `infra`, which Kubernetes' own search path (`cache.prod.svc.cluster.local`) would never reach. The branch is also inconsistent with the ≥2-candidate case, which refuses and drops, and the justifying comment ("so a file whose manifests are vague about namespaces still resolves the way it always did") is inaccurate — a single-namespace file is already satisfied by the preceding `perNamespace.has(readerNamespace)` branch, so the fallback only ever fires when reader and target are in different namespaces.

`configMaps` is still keyed by bare `metadata.name` with no namespace, so the exact collision the item describes for `hostToEntity` survives one layer upstream: two same-named ConfigMaps in a multi-namespace stream overwrite each other (last document silently wins), and a workload's `envFrom.configMapRef` then reads another namespace's values, producing `Calls`/`Depends on` edges from env that is not in that pod at all.

The new `name.namespace` title is collapsed by `normalizeTitle` (which strips `.`), so a qualified title shares a dedup key with a hyphenated name: a stream holding `cache` in `prod` and `team-b` plus a separate workload named `cache-prod` normalizes both to `cacheprod`, dropping one as a "duplicate entity within the same file" and retargeting its edges onto the other — and against the workspace roster, `cache.prod` can match an unrelated existing `cache-prod` as `exact-normalized-title`, proposing an update to the wrong entity.
